Class KeyedStorages

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.storage.KeyedStorages
public final class KeyedStorages extends Object
Factories for KeyedStorage, a Storage that declares its own PersistentContainerKey so per-slot state persists for registered slots.

The player-scoped factory is the supported way to register player-owned storage (pockets or equipment slots, say) with per-slot state. It wraps a content Storage (usually bound from a StorageAttachment) and tags it with a PersistentContainerKey.Modded key whose payload names the owning player. ContainerIdentity routes the registered slot to this key, and the server resolves it to a bag on the player keyed by resolver id, so different slots and different mods never collide.

The library owns the payload shape. These keys are made by the library, unlike the opaque payloads consumers define for their own modded resolvers. The constants below are the contract between this factory and SlotStateServer's Modded resolution.

  • Method Details

    • player

      public static KeyedStorage player(Storage backing, net.minecraft.resources.Identifier resolverId, UUID playerId)
      Wraps backing as a player-scoped KeyedStorage. The returned storage passes all content operations to backing and reports a stable PersistentContainerKey.Modded key for (resolverId, playerId), so per-slot state written on the registered slots persists on the player under resolverId.

      The key is equal on client and server (same resolver id, same payload), as KeyedStorage requires.

      Parameters:
      backing - the content storage (e.g. POCKETS.bind(player))
      resolverId - stable identity of this slot (e.g. "inventory-plus:pockets"); namespaces the bag
      playerId - the owning player's UUID
